title: SK Hynix Profit Jumps Sevenfold to Record on AI Memory Demand
excerpt: Operating profit hit 83.3 trillion won in the third quarter as HBM4 shipments and server memory demand pushed revenue past 100 trillion won for the first time, and the Nvidia supplier unveiled a 100 trillion won shareholder return plan.
body:
• SK Hynix reported third-quarter operating profit of 83.3 trillion won ($62.8 billion), up 632% from 11.4 trillion won a year earlier and above the 76.7 trillion won LSEG SmartEstimate.
  • Revenue rose 328% to 104.6 trillion won, topping 100 trillion won in a quarter for the first time, with a record operating margin of 79.7%.
  • The company announced shareholder returns of about 100 trillion won ($75.4 billion) this year, including 30 trillion won in dividends and 60 trillion won in buybacks and cancellations.
  • SK Hynix said demand will continue to exceed supply through 2030 and that long-term agreements with 14 major customers already cover more than 50% of its 2027 and 2028 production capacity.

SK Hynix reported a more than sevenfold rise in quarterly operating profit to a record high on Wednesday, beating market forecasts as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure drove up memory chip prices, according to Reuters. The South Korean chipmaker, a key supplier to Nvidia, is the clearest earnings signal yet of how much of the AI build-out's value is pooling in memory.

Record Numbers

Operating profit for the July-September period reached 83.33 trillion won, compared with 11.4 trillion won a year earlier, the company said in a regulatory filing. Revenue rose 328% year on year to 104.6 trillion won, surpassing the previous quarterly record set only one quarter earlier, and net profit climbed 214% to 39.53 trillion won. The operating margin of 79.7% was the highest in the company's history, rising from about 72% in the first quarter and 76.3% in the second.

Both headline figures beat expectations. The Korea JoongAng Daily reported that revenue topped a FnGuide consensus of 98.23 trillion won and operating profit beat a 76.96 trillion won consensus. Sales of DRAM chips rose as shipments of the company's latest high-bandwidth memory, HBM4, got into full swing and server memory demand grew, while NAND flash sales increased on solid-state drives for data centers.

Shareholder Returns and Locked-In Demand

Alongside the results, SK Hynix said it will pursue shareholder returns totalling about 100 trillion won this year, comprising cash dividends of 30 trillion won and share repurchases and cancellations of 60 trillion won, including 40 trillion won announced in August. The scale of the return program underlines how quickly AI memory profits have converted into cash.

The company also reiterated that it expects demand to continue to exceed supply through 2030. To improve visibility, SK Hynix has signed long-term agreements with 14 major customers and is discussing extending contract terms, which are typically five years. The volume secured so far corresponds to more than 50% of total production capacity for 2027 and 2028, the company said.

What It Means

By operating profit, the quarter puts SK Hynix among the most profitable technology companies in the world, a position built almost entirely on its lead in high-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators. For investors, the results test a familiar question: whether memory, historically the most cyclical corner of semiconductors, has genuinely become a contracted, multi-year business. The long-term agreements and the demand-exceeds-supply guidance through 2030 are the company's argument that it has.

SK Hynix shares rose 2% on the results, broadly in line with the wider market's 2.2% gain. Attention now turns to how rivals Samsung Electronics and Micron respond, and whether HBM pricing holds as new capacity comes online.
